```Refusing to draft a proposal on the forums goes against all World Assembly etiquette and sets a dangerous precedent for individuals with influence in the WA pushing through resolutions without scrutiny or diverse perspectives. Quorum raiding and queue stuffing were cited as concerns but quorum raiding is not prevented by failing to draft on the forums, as it takes place after submission anyway. Meanwhile, queue stuffing is not a legitimate concern since this is not a time-sensitive resolution either, like a Liberation or Injunction, where this argument would make sense. Some of the criticisms the proposal raises, such as the mention of a one-nation operation in Osiris, make sense, but others do not, as the authors would have heard had they respected the traditional process of drafting. Calling streak-breaking raids "largely inconsequential" is particularly tone deaf when one considers how those raids disrupt the stability of entire communities, and that those raids are mechanically identical to the 2022 attack on The North Pacific, which itself elicited interregional disapproval and condemnation. If a region's sovereignty is violated and the community suffers, foreigners have no right to call it "inconsequential" – it seems more like a Raider argument than a Defender one. Furthermore, The Black Hawks are far from mediocre – they are a significant part of NationStates history, which SC#217 captures. The East Pacific might not be so firm on that stance if the authors had allowed public comment and debate, which is the true arena by which resolutions are refined and strengthened. However, that did not happen, so we are forced to make judgments on elements that might have been changed if constructive dissent had been given an ear. The East Pacific will vote AGAINST this resolution.```
